body.title: Implement targeted daemon-crash fences and local clearance
body.summary: Implement request-scoped resourceGuard discovery across retained attempts and explicit resourceClearance on existing code resume/design recover paths. Bind normal existing broker decisions to exact review/guard/lease sets, persist the receipt via a metadata-only recovery worker and require a separate subsequent review resume.
acceptanceChecks: An unresolved previous-daemon lease or interrupted legacy active attempt with missing guard reconstructs only that review's fence before native work; PID absence cannot clear it.

Existing broker/client authentication is unchanged: valid human-UI and automated local-client answers are equally accepted; caller-provided receipts and stale/wrong-review/lease-set approval are refused.
No-client, decline, expiry, disconnect, lost pending broker request or changed guard state retains the fence. Re-read all unresolved retained-attempt guards before applying a decision.
Persist exact bounded request/guard/lease approval receipt and authorized closure idempotently; metadata-only recovery cannot call native tools/providers or grant artifact approval.
Disposable full-daemon-crash tests keep a surviving old child fenced, allow unrelated reviews, and permit work only after clearance plus explicit resume; never crash the live user daemon.
Partial clearance leaves remaining leases blocking; repeated clearances and response-loss replay preserve audit evidence without duplicate inference.
